### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **10** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/rest/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

- `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`  _(via getBookTree (sdk, the bare tail of client method meta.getBookTree, bound to GET /api/v1/meta/book/:name/tree), meta.getBookTree (sdk, the route ledger binds it to GET /api/v1/meta/book/:name/tree, selected by route anchor /book/:name/tree), meta.publishItem (sdk, the route ledger binds it to POST /api/v1/meta/:type/:name/publish, selected by route anchor /:type/:name/publish), publishItem (sdk, the bare tail of client method meta.publishItem, bound to POST /api/v1/meta/:type/:name/publish))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/rest/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **34** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9f0de32a03629a021836d9216dbca86ccdc645f3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `558f54f896a21b36856ba8bc89225e6dc43c8474` — the merge of head `db727d0d1b23908aef12d2d622b223c244b8646a` into base `9f0de32a03629a021836d9216dbca86ccdc645f3`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 558f54f896a21b36856ba8bc89225e6dc43c8474 && git checkout 558f54f896a21b36856ba8bc89225e6dc43c8474
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 9f0de32a03629a021836d9216dbca86ccdc645f3 db727d0d1b23908aef12d2d622b223c244b8646a && git checkout -B drift-repro 9f0de32a03629a021836d9216dbca86ccdc645f3 && git merge --no-ff db727d0d1b23908aef12d2d622b223c244b8646a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9f0de32a03629a021836d9216dbca86ccdc645f3
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 9f0de32a03629a021836d9216dbca86ccdc645f3` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `db727d0d1b23908aef12d2d622b223c244b8646a`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

**Inputs read.** Card #22188 (body and all 6 comments: the cli seat's pointer `6053861206`, triage `6054416999`, the unlock note `6054787159`, the claim `6057144068`, the os-dev-report `6058135495`, the seat's ACCEPT `6058168399`). PR #22265 body, file list (6 files, +409 / −11) and the net diff `origin/main...db727d0d` (merge-base `ffb31fca`, two commits: `a13568b4` the fix, `db727d0d` test-only). The PR head read twice, 10:47Z and 10:55Z: still `db727d0d`, draft, base `main`. Check-runs on the head, below. The seat's claim and ACCEPT were judged, not adopted.

**Public surface, one change.** `packages/rest/src/index.ts` adds exactly one line of export: `export { metaItemPackageBinding } from './rest-server.js'`. The function (`rest-server.ts:1752`) goes `function` to `export function`; its body is unchanged (`typeof raw === 'string' && raw !== '' && raw !== 'all' ? raw : undefined`). No type export, no signature change, nothing removed. The entry already loaded `rest-server.js` (`index.ts:4`, `RestServer`), so the PR body's closure sentence is true. No export ledger or census test names `metaSaveRequestOptions` or this symbol outside the two source files, their changesets and the two parity pin files, so no ledger update was owed. **Right: a purely additive widening of `@objectstack/rest`'s public surface.** `@objectstack/runtime` exports nothing new; it imports the symbol beside `metaSaveRequestOptions` (`meta.ts:76`).

**Answer changes, each judged.** The contract is the one #22128 / PR #22185 stated and pinned: `?package=all` names no package on the `/meta` item doors (its changeset: `GET ?package=all` reads `all` as the save and publish doors read it). The spec declares no meaning for `all`; the list's `packageId` describe is "Filter by owning package", and `all` is no owning package, so "no filter" is what the describe already says. Each door below moves from "forward the literal `all` to the store as a package id" to "read it as no package", with a real package id still scoping (pinned controls).

1. `RestServer` layered read (`:3936`): 404 for a package-bound item becomes the plain read's layers. The layered read is the item read's sibling at the same address; a 404 for an item that exists was a wrong answer, not a refusal of a request shape. **Right, a correction.**
2. `RestServer` list (`:6065`): `[]` becomes the plain list. H2 verified in the pin: the plain list already spans both packages and the env-local overlay, so no package is already "show everything"; the list needs no reading of its own. **Right.**
3. `RestServer` book tree (`:6400`): the implicit empty book of a package called `all` becomes the declared book. **Right.**
4. `RestServer` diagnostics sweep (`:5822`): `scannedItems: 0` becomes the plain sweep. Verified in-family: `getMetaDiagnostics` (`metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts:7986`) runs `getMetaItems({ type, packageId: request.packageId })` per swept type, a list read keyed by package. Triage's direction was every `?package=` reader in the family; the claim named this line for a reading; the fold is disclosed as a deviation and pinned. **Right.**
5. Dispatcher book tree (`:1038`), layered read (`:1093`), list (`:1930`): the same three corrections on the transport behind the `@objectstack/hono` catch-all. #22141's principle, that the two doors serving one route cannot answer it differently, holds. The book tree's old reading already rejected non-strings and empties, so only `all` moves there. **Right.**
6. Dispatcher item branch (`:1264`), one `packageId` for the read, the `?state=draft` read and the `PUT`: the read serves the item with its `_packageId` as the plain read does; the draft read stops answering `404 NO_DRAFT` for an inherited draft (the #22185 correction, now on this host); the `PUT ?package=all` stores the row env-local (`package_id` null) where it stored `package_id: 'all'`. The write change is a parity correction to `RestServer`'s save door, which has folded `all` since before #22185. **Right.**
7. Dispatcher non-string `?package` (an array) now reads as no package where `query?.package || undefined` forwarded it. This is the exported function's declared arm (its docblock and the rest changeset: "a non-string value is not forwarded either"), not a reading this PR invents. Reach: the catch-all flattens its query to one string per name (`adapters/hono/src/index.ts:737`), and the dispatcher plugin mounts no `/meta` route, so no production path hands it an array; on `RestServer`, every door that folds `?package=` sits behind `refuseRepeatedQueryParams` (`:3934`, `:5671`, `:6062`, `:6398`, `:6450`, `:7146`, `:7958`), so no `RestServer` answer moves on an array. **Right as a consequence of the shared fold, and not an accept-set widening needing its own declaration; the pre-existing multiplicity gap is carried to ③.**

**The cache bypass left raw (`:6600`, `packageScoped`).** It asks only whether the raw parameter is present, to pick the uncached arm; that arm reads through the fold (`:6865`, #22185) and serves `version`. Folding the presence check would send `?package=all` to the cached arm, which serves no `version`, and would break #22185's pinned rows ("active: the read's version is the token the save compares against" under `?package=all`; its changeset: "`?package=all` still takes the uncached arm, so it keeps serving `version`"). The fold's docblock (`:1748`) now records why. **Right.** One note, not a defect: the inline comment above `packageScoped` (`:6593`) still gives ADR-0048 scoping as the bypass's only reason; the docblock is the authority and now says the rest.

**Nothing left unfolded.** At head, every `req.query?.package` reader in `rest-server.ts` is a fold (this PR's four, #22185's three) or the presence check; every `query?.package` reader in `meta.ts` is a fold (four). `GET /meta/_drafts` reads `?packageId=` on both hosts (`rest-server.ts:5920`, `meta.ts:1850`), a different parameter. The dispatcher's three-segment routes are `state`, `layers`, `published` and `book/:name/tree`; it has no `publish` branch, so the PR body's "serves no publish" is consistent with the code.

**Truth of the changesets and PR body against the diff.** Rest changeset: the export sentence, the four-door list, the function's contract (`all`, empty, non-string), "the item read, the save and the publish already read it through" (`:6865`, `:7176`, `:7959`), each before/after row, and the unchanged lines (real id still scopes; the bypass reads raw) are each true of the diff and pinned. Runtime changeset: the `PUT` row, the four read branches, "every branch reads through `metaItemPackageBinding` from `@objectstack/rest`", and the unchanged line are true. PR body: "the only new export" true; H3 both readings true; H4 both reasons verified (`meta-save-request.ts` header scopes it to the save's precondition and lifecycle); H5's objectui sha `a58626c8` equals `.objectui-sha` at head; acceptance notes on flattening, `_drafts` and publish verified. H1's base-column measurements and the reverse-verification counts are the dev's claims, consistent with the base code (which did forward the literal) and with the pin file, whose rows count 6 per host x 2 hosts + 1 sweep = 13. Not re-run here, per the brief.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/rest`: **`minor` with `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right.** AGENTS.md rule 3: `yes` takes at least `minor`, one arm from the closed pair. The widening is the one entry export; the door corrections alone would be `patch` (the shape PR #22185's rest changeset took for the item read's `all` fold). Precedent #22141 / PR #22206 graded the same package the same way for `metaSaveRequestOptions`.
- `@objectstack/runtime`: **`patch` with `Clause-②: no` is right.** Its public surface does not move; its answer changes are parity corrections to the contract `RestServer` already keeps. Same grade and declaration as its #22141 changeset.
- PR body line 2 `Clause-②: yes` matches the rest changeset. `Check Changeset` on the head: success. No changeset is breaking, so no ADR-0087 marker is owed.
- The runtime changeset does not spell out the array reading in ① item 7; the rest changeset's description of the function does, and the PR body's acceptance note does. Not a wrong level.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none in the report.
- `out_of_scope_findings[0]`, `GET /meta/_drafts?packageId=`: **answered.** Verified a differently named parameter on both hosts; not a `?package=` reader; not this family. Noted, not filed, is right.
- `out_of_scope_findings[1]`, an array `?package` on the dispatcher: **answered** in ① item 7, and **escalated to the seat**: the dispatcher's lack of a query-multiplicity judgment has now been recorded on two PRs (#22206's acceptance notes, #22265's) without a card. Whether a card is owed for parity with `RestServer`'s `refuseRepeatedQueryParams` is the seat's call; it does not block this PR.
- Deviation, pins in one runtime file: **answered.** The rest leg drives `RestServer`'s real registered handlers over a real store; runtime can import both subjects and rest cannot import the dispatcher; the precedent file took the same shape.
- Deviation, the diagnostics sweep folded under H3: **answered**, verified in-family in ① item 4.
- Deviation, unit tiers at `a13568b4`: **answered.** `db727d0d` adds only one pin row to the new test file; the named pins were re-run at head; CI on the head is the verdict.
- Deviation, the stray gate runner: process hygiene with no effect on the diff; the tree was shown clean after each leg. No action.
- H5, hosted reach NOT MEASURED: the grade is the seat's, not a contract question. The reading that Studio's save folds `all` itself while its layered and draft reads send the raw router value is consistent with the card's named producer, and this PR fixes the read half on both hosts.
- **Escalated, mine:** rows the dispatcher's `PUT ?package=all` bound to the package `all` before this fix are not migrated here. On H2's reading they stay reachable by the plain read and list, which span every package; whether any exist on a hosted store is not measurable from this review. The seat decides whether a sweep card is owed.
- Check-runs on `db727d0d`, read 2026-10-08T10:55:21Z: 33 runs, 28 success, 3 skipped (Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke), 2 in progress (Lint & Repo Gates, Test Core 1/6), 0 failed. Earlier read 10:48:55Z: 31 runs, 18 success, 3 skipped, 10 in progress, 0 failed. Landing waits on the two still running; nothing read contradicts this verdict.
